newsitem.title: INDIA: India forex reserves at comfortable level-RBI.
newsitem.headline: India forex reserves at comfortable level-RBI.

text.p: India's foreign exchange reserves currently stand at a comfortable level, a senior official of the country's central bank said on Friday.

"The present level of external reserves is a source of comfort as it provides a measure of insulation against unforeseen external shocks created by domestic supply shortages," Deputy Governor Y.V Reddy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) told a meeting of forex dealers in Goa.

Additionally, Reddy said, it served to meet precautionary motives and satisfy the need for liquidity, thus instilling confidence in the Indian economy among international investors and financial markets.

The level of foreign exchange reserves rose to $29.8 billion by August 1 this year, equivalent to seven months of imports, Reddy said. This level is equivalent to about 30 months of debt service payments and 5.7 months of payments for import and debt service taken together.

By the end of March, Reddy added, the ratio of short-term debt to the level of reserves amounted to a little over 25 percent, compared to about 100 percent for Indonesia, 50 percent for Argentina, and 25 percent for Malaysia.
"In fact, the level of reserves exceeds the total stock of short-term debt and portfolio flows which taken together constitute little less than 75 percent of the level of reserves," Reddy said.

He added: "In a period of transition, when structural shifts can release strong excess demand or throw up temporary bottlenecks, reserves smoothen the process of change and mitigate pains of adjustment.
"So some addition to reserves in my view would give additional comfort."
